90466.overview:
Fortress is an unauthorised clone of SEGA's Zaxxon, copying many elements of the original game. It was developed by Amcom and published by Pace in 1983 for the BBC Microcomputer.

 

Although, the graphics had to be toned down in quite a major way, the gameplay remained. Fortress followed Zaxxon almost identically with all of the stages mirrored - even the opening wall that you must squeeze through. The problem with Fortress was that it was even harder than Zaxxon. It was incredibly difficult to get involved with the game, as it was truly a challenge to stay alive for more than a minute or so. Despite this, Fortress was something of a one-off for the BBC, with no other software house ever trying to copy the Zaxxon game

90501.overview:
Felix Meets the Evil Weevils is a platform game developed by John Grove and released by Micro Power.

It is the second sequel in the Felix series. This one has nicer graphics than the others and improved gameplay.

90551.overview:
Felix in the Factory is a platform game for home computers developed by John Chaytor and published by Micro Power (a.k.a. Program Power). The game was first released in 1982 for the BBC Micro. It was ported to the Acorn Electron (1983), Commodore 64 (1984) and Memotech MTX (1984). It is the first in a trilogy of Micro Power games featuring the factory worker Felix and was followed by Felix and the Fruit Monsters (a Pac-Man style overhead maze game) and another factory-based platformer, Felix meets the Evil Weevils.

The object of the game is to keep the Generator, in the bottom right of the factory, filled with oil. If the level of oil, shown at the bottom of the screen, gets too low the lights will start to fail and eventually the Generator will stop.
To oil the Generator, you must guide Felix down the ladder, along the conveyor belt, jumping over the packages, up past the Gremlins to the oil can and then back to the Generator. To help you past the Gremlins, use the pitchfork which is hanging on the wall somewhere and run at the Gremlins. You should be able to knock them off the conveyors.
Another hazard of the factory is the Rat. This will run across a level from time to time. A bag of rat poison is provided to help you reduce the rodent population and you can leave this on any level that you wish.
You can only carry one object at a time and once you have the oil can, you cannot drop it again.
If you trip over the packages on the conveyor belt you will be given a chance to get up again but if you reach the edge of the screen, you will lose a life.

90612.overview: Felix and the Fruit Monsters is a video game developed by John Chaytor and released by Micro Power for the BBC Micro and Acorn Electron in 1983. It is a sequel to the earlier game Felix in the Factory. The game is a sort of Pac-Man clone, in which the player moves around a maze collecting fruit and avoiding the fruit monsters. It was not as successful as the earlier Felix game. It was followed by another sequel, Felix Meets the Evil Weevils.

90819.overview:
Firetrack is a vertically scrolling shooter programmed by Nick Pelling, developed by Aardvark Software and published in 1987 by Electric Dreams for the BBC Microcomputer. The game was heavily influenced by the arcade game Star Force.

Superior Software released it 1n 1989 as part of a collection.

Pirates took possession over a part of space and founded eight colonies. The player's mission as Earth's delegate is to destroy them in this vertically scrolling shooter. Each level has to be crossed twice; the first time the goal is to destroy the reactor at the end of the level. Then the colony falls into darkness and the player tries to destroy as many buildings as possible during a second run. Some structures are marked; those give extra points or in some cases an extra life. Those are needed because the pirates are not in the mood to give in without a fight; contact with an enemy ship or missile means instant death.

90929.overview:
42 billion years ago, the Supreme Being being a rather busy chap, sub-contracts the job of Human evolution to Gal-Corps from the planet Maltron. As it was the sixth day and the local pub was soon closing they decided to spend the rest of the evening drinking Tharsberg Special Brew. Next day, worse for wear, their work suffered and to make matters worse the Scroll of Evolution has been broken into 16 pieces and scattered to the four winds. Fast forward to today and Glob while having a drink is transported in front of the Supreme Being who has tasked him to find the pieces and put them back together in the right order.

Future Shock is a side view flick-screen game, where you must move around searching rooms for the pieces of the scroll represented by the letter P before a candle burns to nothing. Glob can only move left or right so has to use the rooms to fall into other rooms to collect the pieces of the scroll. Some rooms has gravity reversed and Glob will float towards the ceiling but after collecting four pieces of the scroll this reverses. There are also lifts that move Glob to higher places in the room and although there are creatures in various rooms, touching them has no effect. Pressing P brings up Puzzle mode where you see the pieces collected and must slide them around in the right order.

91013.overview:
Firebug is a 1-player arcade game for the BBC Micro and Electron.

As the fireman on duty, the player has been called out to a warehouse where a firebug is attempting to burn it down. The warehouse is full of buckets of flammable liquid, and the player's goal is to carry the liquid to the vat of water to keep it safe. The player can pick up fire extinguishers to put out flames, but can only carry liquid or a fire extinguisher at a time. If the fire spreads to a vat of flammable liquid, the temperature raises 10°C, and if the temperature hits 100°C it's game over. The player can climb ladders, walk on platforms, and jump over flames. If the player hits a danger they fall to the bottom of the screen. The player advances to the next level when all vats of flammable liquid are removed from a level.

91410.overview:
Fat Man Sam is a platform game published by Firebird for the BBC Microcomputer.

Guide Sam around the forty screens, avoiding almost everything that moves. In order to exit each screen, Sam will need to collect all the objects that appear, sometimes keys, sometimes sweets, sometimes... who knows?
And watch out for that crusher.
You can only exit a screen when all the objects have been collected and the exit is flashing.

98701.overview:
Frak! is a computer game originally programmed in machine code by Nick Pelling (Orlando) for the BBC Microcomputer and Acorn Electron and developed and published by his own Aardvark Software label in 1984. It was re-issued in budget form by Alternative Software in 1989.

You play the part of Trogg the caveman. Climb the ladders and jump across platforms to collect gems for points and light bulbs for extra time before the lights go out. All the keys must be collected to finish the level and can often only be collected in the right sequence. Each level is about three screens wide and scrolls as you move across it (The Electron version does not scroll but flips screens).

To hinder Troggs progress, there are statues placed in the way across the level which must be removed by firing a yoyo (Troggs only weapon) at them. There are also balloons which rise from the bottom and daggers which fly diagonally downwards from the top

116664.overview:
Frankenstein 2000 is an action game written by Kevin Blake. The player controls a small machine, and travels in Frankenstein's body. The body is divided in several organs - for example the brain, stomach, lungs, etc. Each organ is a small maze, where the player avoids obstacles and activates special devices. Sometimes, travel between organs looks like a simple shoot'em up, where the player shoots various objects. He must be careful to pay attention to 2 "bars" - damage and oxygen.

The original Icon release was for the BBC Micro only; it was re-released in 1988 on the Atlantis label in cassette format for the BBC and Electron.

124171.overview:
In this game, you control the crewman, manoeuvring him around the Space Station as he tries to destroy Alphoids before being destroyed himself - either by the enemy or due to lack of oxygen.

The Space Station is displayed as a large octagon. Although the station is rotating, it is held fixed on the screen, which means that the objects within move in curves rather than straight lines. On the left of the screen the rotation rate of the station is displayed and a monitor displays a trace of the crewman's heartbeat, recorded from his suit's biomonitors. On the right of the screen, his remaining air supply is displayed. 

Acornsoft Free Fall is fully compatible with either keyboard or joysticks and includes a table of high scores.

124400.overview:
Deadly sub-atomic particles are running free in a scientific research centre. It is your job to trap the darting Leptons using a robot craft before your time runs out.

As you move the craft across the screen, a green ion-trail is dragged along behind. When you reach the edge again, the smaller area confined by this green line, is filled in. A Lepton is captured if it is trapped in this area or if 95% of the screen has been filled. A bar running along the bottom of the screen indicates the percentage of the total area remaining to be filled. Enclosed areas are coloured red, but at any time, you can switch to the faster speed and areas so filled are coloured pink.

Higher levels introduce Chasers which move along the borders. A life is lost if you collide with one of these or if a Lepton hits your trail. The number of Leptons and Chasers increases up to a maximum of 5 of each. An extra craft is obtained on completion of the third, sixth and ninth screens.

A good strategy is to build small, narrow pink blocks up the centre of an unfilled area in fast mode and then to finish off using the slower mode to reach the top of the screen and capture the Lepton.

125383.overview:
Freddy's job is to pick all the fruit in Mr. meano's garden. The fruit starts off as seeds and then grows into plants and flowers and finally into large bulbous fruit which is safe to pick. The larger the fruit the more points but if you leave it too late the fruit will go to seed and multiply to form up to four new seeds which themselves start to grow and so on. If you tread on a plant before it is bearing fruit then Mr. Meano will come after you.

Bees emerge from the beehive and chase you. Use the spraycan to knock them out.

The patrolling Crazy Crimson Caterpillar should also be avoided, as should the deadly droppings of the Sparrow.

Sweets and other goodies appear randomly and should be grabbed.

When you have cleared the garden of fruit you move on to the next level. There are nine levels and you can choose any at the game startup. Complete all nine levels to find out what lies beyond.

127037.overview: Fantasia Diamond is a traditional text adventure with static graphics, where the titular diamond, a family heirloom has been stolen and has to be retrieved from a sinister riverside fortress. Along the way, Boris the Masterspy is to be rescued who was imprisoned during a previous attempt to recover the diamond. On the way you encounter elves, pixies, gnomes and an decidedly unfriendly woodcutter. In order to gain strength, you need to eat and drink and your strength determines how many objects you can carry. There is a real-time element to the game where every character takes an action every 15 seconds or so, without regard to your actions. The interface is text driven with split screen graphics. The text parser can use relatively complex sentences for the time.

127398.overview: Tomcat is a vertically scrolling top-down shooter set in the near future. You can pick up weapon upgrades (more guns, missiles) from destroyed enemies.

127454.overview: Frogger (aka Froggy) is Superior's version of the classic frog crossing the road action game,

137299.overview: Fire Hawks is a 2D shooter in which the player controls a cannon and must shoot the fire hawks. He must stop them before one reaches the bottom of the screen and turns into the phoenix. The battlefield has many obstacles and the player must sometimes destroy several obstacles in order to shoot at the enemy.

138284.overview: The football management game style has been one of the most enduring since Kevin Toms pioneered it in 1982. You start in the 4th division with the team of your choice, and can play on indefinitely in the hope of reaching the top division and dominating it, as well as winning the cups. Players can be bought or sold, with their transfer values varying according to the size of any bid. Their skills and morale vary as the season goes on, with resting key players in easy matches often a key move. You can take out a loan, limited depending on your division, while day-to-day bills must be covered. Matches feature short animated highlights sequences of key moments.

138464.overview: In Footballer of the Year you take control of the career of an aspiring striker with a Division 4 team, with the Footballer of the Year award the ultimate goal. You start with a small amount of money, which is used to buy goal cards; each of these sets you up a chance in a match. Up to three can be played in each game, making Hat-Tricks a possibility.

153234.overview: A clone of Carnival, where you must shoot the fairground targets before the ducks reach the bottom row and devour your bullets.

153235.overview:
Footer is a two player game, the object of which is to score as many goals as possible against your opponent in the time limit of 300 seconds. 
The whistle will be blown once to indicate each kick-off and three times to indicate the end of the match. Typing in RUN (RETURN) at the end of a game will start a new match.

153236.overview: Fruit Machine is a three wheel simulation of slot machine for one player with options such as hold, nudge, gamble, collect and so on.

167568.overview:
You are a British war-time pilot shot down over occupied France. You are taken captive and subsequently escape. In your efforts to make your way back to England your only contact is with the local people who unfortunately speak nothing but French. 
The game consists of four sections which are of increasing difficulty. On each route, you come up against situations (meeting people, buying things, etc) in which you have to reply to questions in French or carry out actions described in French. You have to try and pass as a Frenchman. Listen carefully to all of the characters who speak French, because the Nazis make mistakes.

167584.overview: A two player graphical word strategy game involving matching cartoons and music displayed on screen to gradually reveal hidden words.

167698.overview:
You are P.I. Dan Diamond.
You receive an unsigned letter. Inside is an address, and a message: "Please come, you're our only hope". 
On arrival, you trigger a mechanism, and find yourself falling. Suddenly you are in Franklin's Tomb, and the adventure begins. 
The screen is split into three different coloured sections. One section gives a description of your surroundings, another lists your possessions and the last is for commands, computer responses and articles to be found as you enter a location.

167864.overview:
A text adventure with just a two word parser. It seems to be based on the Doctor Who games, apparently without the BBC's consent!

You are about to take part in an adventure in the Death Zone on Gallifrey. As you were passing through this plastic model, you heard about the abundance of Grassy plains. Your mission is to try to destroy four Doctors before they reach Rassilon’s Tower. Being the MASTER, can you achieve your evil aim and win 13 more regenerations! You are likely to meet evil aliens, problems and even a large hairy Yeti! To be successful you must realize that everything in the adventure has a purpose, and should, in a small way, help you in trying to complete your mission.

Based on the final story in season 21 (1984) of Doctor Who.

171922.overview:
Fruit Machine (aka Bandit) is a one-arm bandit simulation.

Honest Joe is a used car dealer simulation.

192888.overview:
Published in the February 1984 issue of Personal Computer World magazine (PCW).

The listing was for the ORIC-1 computer.

A version for the Commodore 64 was published in Your Commodore magazine in February 1985 under the title of "The Forest of Evil"

Ported to the BBC Micro in June 2020 by the same guy who did the C64 version. The port includes some tweaks, adjustments and general attempts at bugfixing!

199917.overview:
Version of the classic arcade game written by Richard Broadhurst (Tricky) and released as a free download via Retro Software in 2016 for the BBC Micro. 

Supports the VideoNuLA upgrade, which offers the arcade colour palette on the BBC Micro.

205969.overview: A colourful text-based football strategy game in which you must navigate your team to the top of the first division. Pick your team, buy new players, change players and try to win some matches.

206073.overview: You must manoeuvre a man around a maze collecting fruit and the key to the door to the next level. A number of creatures also live in the maze and they make your job much more difficult. You can shoot the creatures when you move sideways but not if they are above or below you. If you manage to escape each level, bonus points are awarded on the time taken and the fruit collected. There are 12 levels in all and each one is harder than the last.

206650.overview: A text adventure written by David Featley and Mark Cook in which the wizard is dying, and you must recover five magical stones to restore him to health.

206910.overview:
A compilation of 4 Audiogenic games. It was released on both cassette and floppy disk formats:

Omega Orb
a single player arcade adventure by Peter Scott. It was originally published by Audiogenic in 1987 and later reissued by Atlantis.

Psycastria 2
a horizontally scrolling shooter for up to 4 players by Gary Partis. A sequel to Psycastria, it was originally published by Audiogenic in 1988 and later reissued by Atlantis.
Note that the box front of the cassette version had the game misnamed as Psycastria. The back cover as well as the actual cassette had it correctly titled as Psycastria 2.

Sphere of Destiny 2
a single player ball control game by Gary Partis. A sequel to Sphere of Destiny, it was first published as part of this compilation.
Note that the box front of the cassette version had the game misnamed as Sphere of Destiny. The back cover as well as the actual cassette had it correctly titled as Sphere of Destiny 2.

Thunderstruck II: The Mindmaster
a single player arcade adventure by Peter Scott. A sequel to Thunderstruck, it was originally published by Audiogenic in 1986.

207186.overview: A clone of Carnival, where you must shoot the fairground targets before the ducks reach the bottom row and devour your bullets.

216019.overview: You have been asked by a dying alien race from across the Universe to search for various amount of treasures scattered around, and return them to save them. In this graphic text adventure you see text describing each location and you can see a picture showing you what each location looks like. You type in commands with the keyboard to interact with the locations and control your hero.

218226.overview: You must get the enemy in your crosshairs if you expect to survive the adrenaline filled dogfight in the skies.

218227.overview: A football game, that was also released under the name "Star Socca".

218229.overview: A 1982 educational game for the BBC Micro that quizzes the player on his/her knowledge of various flags.

218231.overview:
Billed as 'The first real Fruit Machine Simulator' this is a game for 1 - 4 players that starts you off with £1.50p and sets about helping the player lose it.

Though not based on a specific machine, it has features that fruit machines of the 1980's had such as Cash Box, Nudge Box, Skill Climb, Winning Streak, Cash Gamble, Hold, Mega-hold, and more.

The money that the player has is represents as a number of coins, £1, 50p, 20p, and 10p. The player selects which coins to feed into the machine by the number keys. All stakes are 10p. After entering the coins, game-play is a simple matter of pressing the space bar to spin the reels and see whether a winning combination comes up.

Whenever a win is awarded the player gets the option to either gamble the win or to take the cash. Feature wins Some symbols on the reels have numbers on them. Should these appear on the winning line the letters of the CASH BASH light up. Rarely these letters light up part way and stay lit for the next spin. Other symbols have a '?' on them, these trigger a feature in which all the unlit letters of the CASH BASH feature flash randomly and the player has to stop them flashing at a time when all are lit. If, by either means, all the letters of this feature light up the player gets a chance at the bonus features. There are four of these and they represented by flashing lights, the player stops the lights flashing and is awarded the corresponding lit feature.

The Skill Climb starts with four columns of lights representing coins, column 1 is 10p's, column 2 is 20p's, column 3 is 50p's and column 4 is £1's The lights flash on and off and the player must stop them flashing by pressing an action key. If the player stops the lights at the bottom of the column then they lose If the player stops the lights part way up the column then they win an amount equivalent to all the lights lit If the player stops the lights at the top of the column then the player progresses to the next column where the coins are worth more and the lights flash faster.

The Cash Box is an sum of money that builds during play and is awarded should the player select this feature

The Nudge Box is a number of nudges that builds during play and is awarded should the player select this feature

The Winning Streak is a series of spins each one guaranteed to win something

Randomly throughout the game reels can be held or nudged. Rarely, reels can be held after a win.

218724.overview:
Beeb-Darts (also known as Flights of Fancy) is a 1-2 player darts game for the BBC Micro. It was developed by M.J. Parrot and published as a type-in game in the following:

-   Your Computer magazine, volume 3, issue 5, in May 1983.

-   Your Computer magazine, volume 6, issue 5, in May 1986.

419504.overview: A Reversi style board game where 2 players can play against each another, or a single player can play against the computer.

419532.overview:
A text adventure with graphics featuring sound effects, music and real-time game Save and Reload.
In your search for the legendary Flint's Gold you will sail the Spanish Maine to a land of bloodthirsty pirates.

419771.overview:
The A&F version of the classic arcade game that tasks you with helping some frogs cross a busy freeway and a dangerous river.

An early release on the BBC Microcomputer prior to the more stringent application of intellectual property rights.

419810.overview:
Number 1 in the Firienwood adventure series.

An evil wizard has captured the magic Golden Bird Of Paradise and has imprisoned it in a weird castle in the middle of the enchanted Firien Wood.
Your quest is to find the bird and set it free, in return for its freedom the bird will give you health, wealth and prosperity. You will need magic to overcome the wizard's powers and before you can enter Firien Wood safely, you will need to find a magic lamp.

420151.overview:
This game involves you crossing a busy road full of racing cars, buggies, bulldozers and lorries, to the central bank; then crossing a fast-flowing river with turtles and logs, to the safety of your froghole.
Each frog has twenty seconds to reach the safety of it's bay. When five frogs are safely home, the game restarts on a harder level. After each game, the top ten scores are displayed including your own if you reach 500 or more points.

Froggy was programmed by 3 Northumbrian Prudhoe Community High School 6th formers, Jeffrey, Stephen and David, and published on their own JSD Software label.

420575.overview: An arcade fruit machine simulation featuring Catcher Maze, Jackpot Win, Mystery Win, Feature Hold, Free-Spin, Hold, Money Squares, Gamble, Nudge, Boost.

421082.overview: A slot machine simulation with all the expected features including collect, gamble, hold, mystery spin, nudge and more.

421500.overview: A Fruit Machine simulation featuring sound, spinning reels, five row by four column display of fruit, win-line, "bounce" as each reel settles, nudge box, nudge, gambles, two way nudges, swap reels, hold reels, collect win, gamble win, "loser's gamble" if the first gamble is lost, super gamble for the jackpot, and a coin pile that shrinks and grows with your winnings.

422294.overview:
A five game compendium of games previously published as standalone titles.

Combat Lynx: an action flight simulation by Nick Wilson and Julian Todd, originally released in 1985 by Durell Software

Death Star: a scrolling space shooter by Peter Johnson, originally released in 1985 by Superior Software. 

Geoff Capes Strong Man: a multi event sports game by Michael Archer and David Wainwright, originally released in 1984 by Martech Games

Repton: a scrolling maze game by Tim Tyler, originally released in 1985 by Superior Software.

Twin Kingdom Valley: an adventure game with graphics by Trevor Hall, originally released in 1983 by Bug-Byte Software

422347.overview:
A seven game compilation of games originally published as stand alone titles. The final part of Beau Jolly's Five Star Games series.

Caveman Capers: a single player platformer by Kevin Blake and Jason Sobell, originally released by Icon in 1985.

Frak!: a single player platformer by Nick Pelling, originally released by Aardvark in 1984.

Project Thesius: a single player text adventure by Robert and Mike O'Leary, originally released by Robico in 1986.

Southern Belle: a single player railways simulation by Hewson Consultants, originally released by the developer in 1987.

Strike Force Harrier: a single player combat flight simulator by Ron Hyde, originally released by Mirrorsoft in 1985.

The Way Of The Exploding Fist: a fighting game for up to two players by Michael Simpson, originally released by Melbourne House in 1985.

Thunderstruck: a single player platform adventure by Peter Scott, originally released by Audiogenic Software in 1985.

422352.overview:
A five game compilation of games originally published as stand alone titles. Part two of Beau Jolly's Five Star Games series.

Galaforce: a single player Galaga variant by Kevin Edwards and Martin Galway, originally released by Superior/Acornsoft in 1986.

Karate Combat: a fighting game for up to 2 players by Martin Sykes, originally released by Superior Software in 1986.

Moon Mission: a single player Lunar Rescue variant by Andrew Harley, originally released by Superior Software in 1984.

Stock Car: a top down car racing game for up to two players by A. W. Halse, originally released by Micro Power in 1983.

Thrust: a single player scrolling shooter by Jeremy Smith, originally released by Superior Software in 1986.

439118.overview:
This was the featured game on the Micro User cassette, volume 3, issue 5. It was known as Mutant Fly on the boxart, and as Fly in-game.

You must trap the fly by surrounding it with bricks. The fly can only destroy the bricks when you drive them straight at it. Beware of moving the bricks too close to the edge.

457138.overview:
This is a flight simulator type of game, with the whole basis being your ability to use the keyboard to control the preparation, take-off, flight and landing of the tri-star jet to various destinations.

The following instructions will explain the controls, but purposely, you will not be told how to use the controls or in which exact order, as the whole game is an exercise in logic and skill.

Always bear in mind that certain things have to be done in a certain order. For instance, the safety devices on the plane most certainly will not let you take your brakes off whilst the doors are open or allow you to raise the wheels whilst still on the ground.

457157.overview:
Right, if you're new to the Flying game CONCENTRATE!

Your aircraft is in level flight, to climb pull back, to descend push forward.

You will notice that speed increases in a dive & decreases in a climb.

This is because the thrust is set for level flight.

457207.overview: If the fruits only appear in the first and middle reels only half the amount is paid. To start with.... I'll lend you 50p... but I want it back!

457552.overview:
The Fall of Rome is a turn-based strategy game set during the decline of the Roman Empire, beginning in 395 AD. Players assume control of the empire, managing its provinces and military forces to withstand invasions from barbarian tribes and neighboring powers over a series of 12 turns, each representing five years, culminating in 450 AD.

Gameplay is divided into three phases per turn: recruitment, movement, and combat. During recruitment, players allocate provincial income to raise new forces, choosing between mobile legions and static legions—the latter being less costly but immobile. The movement phase allows the redistribution of armies and treasury between adjacent provinces. In the combat phase, battles are resolved automatically, with outcomes based on the composition and positioning of forces. Additional units, such as cavalry and auxilia, can be recruited temporarily under specific conditions.

The game's interface is primarily text-based, supplemented by a simple map depicting the empire and surrounding regions, divided into provinces. The original packaging included a printed map to assist with strategic planning.

457576.overview:
First Moves is an educational program designed to teach the basic rules and strategies of chess. Aimed at beginners, the software introduces players to piece movements, game objectives, and foundational tactics through a structured series of lessons.

The program features a virtual chessboard where users can interactively practice moves, solve exercises, and receive feedback. Lessons cover key concepts such as check and checkmate, legal moves, castling, and simple openings. It includes guided scenarios that help players understand both the mechanics and strategy of the game.

457577.overview:
Flash is a memory-based reaction game where players are challenged to recall and replicate sequences of flashing blocks displayed in the four corners of the screen. Each block corresponds to a specific key. After observing the sequence, players must input the correct order using these keys. The game tests both memory and reaction time, with increasing difficulty as sequences become longer and input time decreases.

Flash was also featured in the 'Arcade Action' compilation.

457586.overview:
Fistful of Fun is a compilation of five arcade-style games, two of which debuted in this compilation.

The compilation features the following games:

- 3D Space Raider: A space shooter where players pilot a ship through three-dimensional space, engaging alien vessels and defending bases.
- Bug Blaster: A fixed-screen shooter inspired by Centipede, where players eliminate insect-like enemies descending the screen.
- Growing Pains: An arcade game set in a garden environment, where players must water plants while avoiding hazards like snails and bees.
- Tarzan: A side-scrolling action game featuring jungle-themed challenges.
- Uncle Claude: A top-down arcade game with unique gameplay mechanics.

457647.overview:
Froglet is an arcade game and Frogger clone where the player controls a frog attempting to cross a busy highway and a river to reach safe zones at the top of the screen. The game challenges players to avoid vehicles on the road and navigate floating logs and turtles on the river, with turtles occasionally submerging. Players start with four lives and must successfully occupy all four homes at the top of the screen within a time limit to advance to more difficult levels. 

Froglet was initially published as a type-in listing in the April 1983 issue of Computing Today magazine and later updated in the June 1983 issue. It was subsequently offered for commercial sale by ASP Software.

457651.overview:
F.S.S. Liberator is a scrolling action game in which the player controls a spacecraft on a mission to recover the stolen F.S.S. Columbus, a prototype starcruiser capable of intergalactic travel. The Columbus is believed to be hidden near the core of a heavily fortified outlaw planet named Meganorma. The player pilots the F.S.S. Liberator through hostile terrain in an effort to locate and reclaim the missing vessel.

Gameplay involves maneuvering the ship in all directions across a rightward-scrolling screen, avoiding incoming missiles and deploying bombs to destroy enemy energy supplies. Destroying these supplies replenishes the ship's fuel reserves, which are necessary for survival. Each level ends when all energy supplies are eliminated, allowing progression to the next stage. If the ship runs out of fuel or is hit, the game ends.
